description: Cybersecurity question bank derived from FDA/SDA Computer Knowledge 19.9 Cybersecurity notes (293 questions). Verify before formal examination use.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is cybersecurity?

options.A: The practice of protecting computers, networks, applications, devices and data from unauthorised access, attacks, damage and disruption
options.B: The process of installing antivirus software on a single computer
options.C: A method of encrypting all files on a network
options.D: A law that governs internet usage in India

questions.explanation: Cybersecurity is the practice of protecting computers, networks, applications, devices and data from unauthorised access, attacks, damage and disruption.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is the main objective of cybersecurity?

options.A: To increase internet speed
options.B: To protect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of information and information systems
options.C: To reduce the cost of software
options.D: To eliminate all computer viruses permanently

questions.explanation: The main objective is to protect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of information and information systems.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What are the three components of the CIA triad?

options.A: Control, Inspection, Audit

questions.explanation: The CIA triad consists of Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is confidentiality in information security?

options.A: Ensuring information is always available
options.B: Ensuring information is accurate and complete
options.C: Ensuring information is accessible only to authorised people, systems or processes
options.D: Ensuring information is backed up daily

questions.explanation: Confidentiality means ensuring that information is accessible only to authorised people, systems or processes.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is integrity in information security?

options.A: Maintaining the accuracy, completeness and trustworthiness of information and preventing unauthorised alteration
options.B: Ensuring only authorised users can view data
options.C: Ensuring systems are available when needed

questions.explanation: Integrity means maintaining the accuracy, completeness and trustworthiness of information and preventing unauthorised alteration.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is availability in information security?

options.A: Ensuring only authorised users can access information
options.C: Ensuring information and systems are accessible to authorised users when required

questions.explanation: Availability means ensuring that information and systems are accessible to authorised users when required.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is information security?

options.A: The protection of information and information systems against unauthorised access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification or destruction
options.B: The process of installing a firewall
options.C: A software used to detect viruses

questions.explanation: Information security is the protection of information and information systems against unauthorised access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification or destruction.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is the difference between cybersecurity and information security?

options.A: They are exactly the same
options.B: Cybersecurity focuses on protecting digital systems and cyberspace; information security is broader and protects information in digital, physical and other forms
options.C: Information security is narrower than cybersecurity

questions.explanation: Cybersecurity focuses on protecting digital systems and cyberspace; information security is broader and protects information in digital, physical and other forms.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is a cyber threat?

options.A: A potential event or action that could exploit a vulnerability and cause harm to a system, network or data

questions.explanation: A cyber threat is a potential event or action that could exploit a vulnerability and cause harm to a system, network or data.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is a cyberattack?

options.A: A security policy document
options.B: A deliberate attempt to compromise the confidentiality, integrity or availability of a system, network or information

questions.explanation: A cyberattack is a deliberate attempt to compromise the confidentiality, integrity or availability of a system, network or information.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is a vulnerability?

options.A: A weakness in software, hardware, configuration, process or human behaviour that may be exploited
options.B: A confirmed attack on a system

questions.explanation: A vulnerability is a weakness in software, hardware, configuration, process or human behaviour that may be exploited.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is an exploit?

options.A: A technique, code or action that takes advantage of a vulnerability

questions.explanation: An exploit is a technique, code or action that takes advantage of a vulnerability.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is risk in cybersecurity?

options.A: A guaranteed loss
options.B: The possibility of loss or harm when a threat exploits a vulnerability, considered in terms of likelihood and impact

questions.explanation: Risk is the possibility of loss or harm when a threat exploits a vulnerability, considered in terms of likelihood and impact.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is an attack surface?

options.A: The set of points through which an attacker could attempt to enter or affect a system
options.B: The physical surface of a server
options.C: The total number of users in an organisation
options.D: The speed of a network connection

questions.explanation: An attack surface is the set of points through which an attacker could attempt to enter or affect a system.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is a security control?

options.A: A safeguard or measure used to reduce security risk, such as access control, encryption, backups or monitoring

questions.explanation: A security control is a safeguard or measure used to reduce security risk, such as access control, encryption, backups or monitoring.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is defence in depth?

options.A: Using a single strong firewall
options.B: A security strategy that uses multiple layers of safeguards so that failure of one control does not expose the entire system

questions.explanation: Defence in depth is a security strategy that uses multiple layers of safeguards so that failure of one control does not expose the entire system.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is a security policy?

options.A: A formal set of rules and requirements governing how an organisation protects and uses its information systems
options.B: A software program that blocks viruses

questions.explanation: A security policy is a formal set of rules and requirements governing how an organisation protects and uses its information systems.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is an incident in cybersecurity?

options.A: A scheduled maintenance activity
options.B: An event that actually or potentially compromises the confidentiality, integrity or availability of systems or information

questions.explanation: An incident is an event that actually or potentially compromises the confidentiality, integrity or availability of systems or information.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is incident response?

options.A: The organised process of preparing for, detecting, containing, eradicating and recovering from security incidents, followed by lessons learned
options.B: The process of installing antivirus software

questions.explanation: Incident response is the organised process of preparing for, detecting, containing, eradicating and recovering from security incidents, followed by lessons learned.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is the difference between authentication and authorisation?

options.A: They mean the same thing
options.B: Authentication verifies identity; authorisation determines what an authenticated identity is permitted to do
options.C: Authorisation verifies identity; authentication determines permissions
options.D: Authentication is only for passwords; authorisation is only for biometrics

questions.explanation: Authentication verifies identity; authorisation determines what an authenticated identity is permitted to do.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is malware?

options.A: Malicious software designed to damage, disrupt, spy on, exploit or gain unauthorised access to computers, networks or data

questions.explanation: Malware is malicious software designed to damage, disrupt, spy on, exploit or gain unauthorised access to computers, networks or data.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What does the term malware mean?

options.A: Malicious software

questions.explanation: Malware is short for malicious software.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is the main purpose of malware?

options.A: To improve system performance
options.B: To perform unauthorised or harmful actions, such as stealing information, disrupting systems, spying, encrypting files or giving attackers access

questions.explanation: The main purpose of malware is to perform unauthorised or harmful actions, such as stealing information, disrupting systems, spying, encrypting files or giving attackers access.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: Name common types of malware.

options.A: Viruses, worms, Trojan horses, ransomware, spyware, adware, rootkits, keyloggers, bots and backdoors

questions.explanation: Common types of malware include viruses, worms, Trojan horses, ransomware, spyware, adware, rootkits, keyloggers, bots and backdoors.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is a computer virus?

options.A: A type of malware that attaches itself to a host file or program and replicates when the infected host is executed
options.B: A standalone program that spreads over networks without a host
options.C: Software that disguises itself as legitimate software
options.D: A program that encrypts files and demands payment

questions.explanation: A computer virus is a type of malware that attaches itself to a host file or program and replicates when the infected host is executed.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is a computer worm?

options.A: A virus that attaches to a host file
options.B: A standalone type of malware that can self-replicate and spread between systems, often by exploiting network or software weaknesses
options.C: A program that disguises itself as legitimate software
options.D: A program that encrypts files and demands payment

questions.explanation: A computer worm is a standalone type of malware that can self-replicate and spread between systems, often by exploiting network or software weaknesses.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is a Trojan horse?

options.A: A standalone worm that spreads across networks
options.B: Malware that disguises itself as legitimate or useful software to trick a user into installing or running it
options.C: A virus that infects the boot sector
options.D: A program that encrypts files and demands payment

questions.explanation: A Trojan horse is malware that disguises itself as legitimate or useful software to trick a user into installing or running it.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is ransomware?

options.A: Malware that blocks access to systems or data, commonly by encrypting files, and demands payment for restoration or non-disclosure
options.B: Software that secretly monitors user activity

questions.explanation: Ransomware is malware that blocks access to systems or data, commonly by encrypting files, and demands payment for restoration or non-disclosure.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is spyware?

options.A: Software that displays advertisements
options.B: Software that secretly monitors a user's activity or collects information without appropriate knowledge or consent
options.C: Software that encrypts files and demands payment

questions.explanation: Spyware is software that secretly monitors a user's activity or collects information without appropriate knowledge or consent.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is adware?

options.A: Software that secretly monitors user activity
options.B: Software that displays advertising; malicious or intrusive adware may track users, change browser settings or expose them to unwanted content
options.C: Software that encrypts files and demands payment

questions.explanation: Adware is software that displays advertising; malicious or intrusive adware may track users, change browser settings or expose them to unwanted content.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is a rootkit?

options.A: Malicious software or a set of tools designed to conceal malicious activity and maintain privileged or persistent access to a system

questions.explanation: A rootkit is malicious software or a set of tools designed to conceal malicious activity and maintain privileged or persistent access to a system.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is a keylogger?

options.A: Software or hardware that records keystrokes, potentially capturing passwords and other sensitive information

questions.explanation: A keylogger is software or hardware that records keystrokes, potentially capturing passwords and other sensitive information.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is a backdoor in cybersecurity?

options.A: A hidden or unauthorised method of bypassing normal authentication or security controls to access a system
options.B: A physical entrance to a server room

questions.explanation: A backdoor is a hidden or unauthorised method of bypassing normal authentication or security controls to access a system.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is a bot in cybersecurity?

options.A: A compromised device or program that can be remotely controlled to perform automated tasks, often as part of a botnet

questions.explanation: A bot is a compromised device or program that can be remotely controlled to perform automated tasks, often as part of a botnet.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is a botnet?

options.A: A network of compromised devices controlled by an attacker, commonly used for spam, distributed denial-of-service attacks or other malicious activity

questions.explanation: A botnet is a network of compromised devices controlled by an attacker, commonly used for spam, distributed denial-of-service attacks or other malicious activity.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is a fileless malware attack?

options.A: An attack that uses legitimate system tools or memory-based techniques to operate while minimising reliance on traditional malicious files
options.B: An attack that deletes all files
options.C: An attack that only targets files

questions.explanation: A fileless malware attack uses legitimate system tools or memory-based techniques to operate while minimising reliance on traditional malicious files.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is a logic bomb?

options.A: Malicious code designed to activate when a specified condition or event occurs

questions.explanation: A logic bomb is malicious code designed to activate when a specified condition or event occurs.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is a time bomb in computing?

options.A: A type of logic bomb that activates at a predetermined time or date

questions.explanation: A time bomb is a type of logic bomb that activates at a predetermined time or date.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is a malicious macro?

options.A: A macro embedded in a document that performs harmful actions when executed

questions.explanation: A malicious macro is a macro embedded in a document that performs harmful actions when executed.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: Can malware spread through email attachments?

options.A: No, email attachments are always safe
options.B: Yes, malicious attachments may infect a device when opened or executed, or when users enable unsafe content such as macros
options.C: Only if the attachment is a .txt file

questions.explanation: Yes. Malicious attachments may infect a device when opened or executed, or when users enable unsafe content such as macros.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: Can malware spread through infected USB drives?

options.A: No, USB drives cannot carry malware
options.B: Yes, removable media can carry malicious files or exploit weaknesses when connected to a device
options.C: Only if the USB drive is new

questions.explanation: Yes. Removable media can carry malicious files or exploit weaknesses when connected to a device.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is a drive-by download?

options.A: A download or installation that occurs without a user's informed intention, sometimes after visiting a compromised or malicious website
options.B: A legitimate software update downloaded from an official source
options.C: A manual download initiated by the user from a trusted app store
options.D: A backup file downloaded from cloud storage

questions.explanation: A drive-by download is a download or installation that occurs without a user's informed intention, sometimes after visiting a compromised or malicious website.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is a potentially unwanted application (PUA)?

options.A: Software that may be unwanted because of intrusive behaviour, bundling, excessive permissions or other undesirable characteristics, even if it is not classified as malware
options.B: A virus that infects boot sectors
options.C: A ransomware program that encrypts files

questions.explanation: A potentially unwanted application (PUA) is software that may be unwanted because of intrusive behaviour, bundling, excessive permissions or other undesirable characteristics, even if it is not classified as malware.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.topic: Virus, Worm, Trojan and Ransomware: Differences
questions.question: What is the main difference between a virus and a worm?

options.A: A virus attaches to a host file or program and usually spreads when that host is run; a worm is standalone and can self-replicate across systems or networks
options.B: A virus self-replicates without a host; a worm needs a host file
options.C: A virus only affects hardware; a worm only affects software

questions.explanation: A virus attaches to a host file or program and usually spreads when that host is run; a worm is standalone and can self-replicate across systems or networks.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.topic: Virus, Worm, Trojan and Ransomware: Differences
questions.question: Does a computer virus normally need a host file or program?

options.A: No, it is always standalone
options.B: Yes, a traditional virus attaches to a host file, program or other host object

questions.explanation: Yes. A traditional virus attaches to a host file, program or other host object.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.topic: Virus, Worm, Trojan and Ransomware: Differences
questions.question: Does a worm require a host file to spread?

options.A: Yes, always
options.B: No, a worm is standalone and can spread independently, often over networks

questions.explanation: No. A worm is standalone and can spread independently, often over networks.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.topic: Virus, Worm, Trojan and Ransomware: Differences
questions.question: How does a Trojan differ from a virus?

options.A: A Trojan disguises itself as legitimate software and relies on deception to get installed or executed; a virus attaches to a host and replicates
options.B: A Trojan self-replicates; a virus does not
options.C: A Trojan only affects hardware; a virus only affects software

questions.explanation: A Trojan disguises itself as legitimate software and relies on deception to get installed or executed; a virus attaches to a host and replicates.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.topic: Virus, Worm, Trojan and Ransomware: Differences
questions.question: Does a Trojan horse self-replicate by definition?

options.A: Yes, always
options.B: No, self-replication is not a defining feature of a Trojan horse
options.D: Only when connected to the internet

questions.explanation: No. Self-replication is not a defining feature of a Trojan horse.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.topic: Virus, Worm, Trojan and Ransomware: Differences
questions.question: What is the defining feature of ransomware?

options.A: It displays advertisements
options.B: It denies access to data or systems, commonly through encryption, and demands payment or another benefit
options.D: It disguises itself as legitimate software

questions.explanation: Ransomware denies access to data or systems, commonly through encryption, and demands payment or another benefit.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.topic: Virus, Worm, Trojan and Ransomware: Differences
questions.question: Can ransomware steal data as well as encrypt it?

options.A: No, ransomware only encrypts files
options.B: Yes, some ransomware operations also steal data and threaten to publish or disclose it
options.C: Only if the victim pays first

questions.explanation: Yes. Some ransomware operations also steal data and threaten to publish or disclose it.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.topic: Virus, Worm, Trojan and Ransomware: Differences
questions.question: What is a macro virus?

options.A: A virus written using an application's macro language that infects documents or templates and may spread when they are opened or used
options.B: A virus that infects the boot sector
options.C: A virus that changes its code as it replicates
options.D: A virus that infects executable files

questions.explanation: A macro virus is a virus written using an application's macro language that infects documents or templates and may spread when they are opened or used.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.topic: Virus, Worm, Trojan and Ransomware: Differences
questions.question: What is a boot-sector virus?

options.A: A virus that infects the boot sector or related startup area of a storage device
options.C: A virus that changes its code as it replicates
options.D: A virus that infects executable files

questions.explanation: A boot-sector virus infects the boot sector or related startup area of a storage device.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.topic: Virus, Worm, Trojan and Ransomware: Differences
questions.question: What is a file-infecting virus?

options.A: A virus that infects the boot sector
options.B: A virus that attaches to executable files or program files and runs when the infected file is executed
options.D: A virus that changes its code as it replicates

questions.explanation: A file-infecting virus attaches to executable files or program files and runs when the infected file is executed.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.topic: Virus, Worm, Trojan and Ransomware: Differences
questions.question: What is a polymorphic virus?

options.A: A virus that changes aspects of its code or appearance as it replicates to make signature-based detection more difficult
options.B: A virus that infects the boot sector
options.D: A virus that remains active in memory

questions.explanation: A polymorphic virus changes aspects of its code or appearance as it replicates to make signature-based detection more difficult.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.topic: Virus, Worm, Trojan and Ransomware: Differences
questions.question: What is a metamorphic virus?

options.A: A virus that changes its appearance without changing its code
options.B: A virus that rewrites or transforms its own code while preserving its malicious behaviour
options.C: A virus that infects the boot sector

questions.explanation: A metamorphic virus rewrites or transforms its own code while preserving its malicious behaviour.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.topic: Virus, Worm, Trojan and Ransomware: Differences
questions.question: What is a multipartite virus?

options.A: A virus that infects more than one type of system target, such as both boot sectors and executable files
options.B: A virus that changes its code as it replicates
options.C: A virus that remains active in memory
options.D: A virus that only infects documents

questions.explanation: A multipartite virus infects more than one type of system target, such as both boot sectors and executable files.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.topic: Virus, Worm, Trojan and Ransomware: Differences
questions.question: What is a resident virus?

options.A: A virus that does not remain active in memory
options.B: A virus that remains active in a computer's memory and may infect files or programs as they are accessed
options.C: A virus that infects the boot sector
options.D: A virus that only infects documents

questions.explanation: A resident virus remains active in a computer's memory and may infect files or programs as they are accessed.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.topic: Virus, Worm, Trojan and Ransomware: Differences
questions.question: What is a non-resident virus?

options.A: A virus that remains active in memory
options.B: A virus that does not remain active in memory and instead infects selected files when executed
options.C: A virus that infects the boot sector
options.D: A virus that changes its code as it replicates

questions.explanation: A non-resident virus does not remain active in memory and instead infects selected files when executed.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.topic: Virus, Worm, Trojan and Ransomware: Differences
questions.question: What is the safest response to a suspected ransomware infection?

options.A: Pay the ransom immediately
options.B: Disconnect the affected device from networks if safe to do so, notify the responsible security team, preserve evidence and follow the organisation's incident-response plan; do not rush to pay
options.C: Delete all files and restart the computer
options.D: Ignore the infection and continue working

questions.explanation: The safest response is to disconnect the affected device from networks if safe to do so, notify the responsible security team, preserve evidence and follow the organisation's incident-response plan; do not rush to pay.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.topic: Virus, Worm, Trojan and Ransomware: Differences
questions.question: Does paying a ransomware demand guarantee file recovery?

options.A: Yes, always
options.B: No, attackers may fail to provide working decryption keys, demand more money or misuse stolen data
options.D: Only if the police are informed

questions.explanation: No. Attackers may fail to provide working decryption keys, demand more money or misuse stolen data.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What are common ways malware enters a computer?

options.A: Malicious email attachments, deceptive links, infected downloads, compromised websites, removable media, vulnerable software and unauthorised applications
options.B: Only through physical theft of the computer

questions.explanation: Common ways malware enters a computer include malicious email attachments, deceptive links, infected downloads, compromised websites, removable media, vulnerable software and unauthorised applications.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: How can phishing deliver malware?

options.A: By automatically installing antivirus software
options.B: A phishing message may persuade a user to open a malicious attachment, download a harmful file or visit a website that exploits a weakness
options.C: By backing up files to the cloud

questions.explanation: A phishing message may persuade a user to open a malicious attachment, download a harmful file or visit a website that exploits a weakness.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: How can outdated software increase malware risk?

options.A: It cannot; outdated software is safe
options.B: Known vulnerabilities may remain unpatched and can be exploited by attackers to install or execute malware

questions.explanation: Known vulnerabilities may remain unpatched and can be exploited by attackers to install or execute malware.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is social engineering?

options.A: The manipulation of people into revealing information or taking actions that compromise security

questions.explanation: Social engineering is the manipulation of people into revealing information or taking actions that compromise security.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is a malicious download?

options.A: A file or application obtained from an untrusted source that contains malware or performs harmful actions
options.B: A file downloaded from an official app store
options.D: A software update from the manufacturer

questions.explanation: A malicious download is a file or application obtained from an untrusted source that contains malware or performs harmful actions.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is software bundling risk?

options.A: An installer may include additional unwanted or malicious software along with the program the user intended to install
options.B: A software package is too large to download
options.C: Software is sold at a discount

questions.explanation: Software bundling risk is that an installer may include additional unwanted or malicious software along with the program the user intended to install.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is a watering-hole attack?

options.A: An attack in which criminals compromise a website frequently visited by a target group to infect or exploit visitors
options.B: An attack on a water treatment plant
options.C: An attack that floods a network with traffic
options.D: An attack that steals passwords through email

questions.explanation: A watering-hole attack is an attack in which criminals compromise a website frequently visited by a target group to infect or exploit visitors.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is a supply-chain attack?

options.A: An attack on a logistics company
options.B: An attack that compromises a supplier, software component, update process or service to reach downstream organisations or users
options.C: An attack that only targets individual home users
options.D: An attack that steals physical goods

questions.explanation: A supply-chain attack compromises a supplier, software component, update process or service to reach downstream organisations or users.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is an unpatched vulnerability?

options.A: A vulnerability that has been fixed
options.B: A known or discovered security weakness for which the relevant fix has not yet been applied to the affected system
options.C: A vulnerability that does not exist

questions.explanation: An unpatched vulnerability is a known or discovered security weakness for which the relevant fix has not yet been applied to the affected system.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is the risk of removable media?

options.A: Automatically launching content from removable media can allow malicious code to run; modern systems restrict such behaviour, but users should still scan and verify media

questions.explanation: Automatically launching content from removable media can allow malicious code to run; modern systems restrict such behaviour, but users should still scan and verify media.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: Why should software be downloaded from official sources?

options.A: Official or verified sources reduce the risk of modified installers, counterfeit applications and bundled malware
options.D: Official sources do not require updates

questions.explanation: Official or verified sources reduce the risk of modified installers, counterfeit applications and bundled malware.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is a malicious browser extension?

options.A: An extension that steals data, injects unwanted content, changes browser behaviour or performs other unauthorised actions

questions.explanation: A malicious browser extension steals data, injects unwanted content, changes browser behaviour or performs other unauthorised actions.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is a compromised website?

options.A: A website that has been shut down
options.B: A legitimate website that has been altered or taken over so that it may distribute malware, host scams or redirect visitors
options.C: A website with a slow connection
options.D: A website that requires a password

questions.explanation: A compromised website is a legitimate website that has been altered or taken over so that it may distribute malware, host scams or redirect visitors.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: Can malware spread through shared network folders?

options.A: No, network folders are always safe
options.B: Yes, if permissions are weak or systems are vulnerable, malware may access or infect files across shared folders

questions.explanation: Yes. If permissions are weak or systems are vulnerable, malware may access or infect files across shared folders.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is phishing?

options.A: A social-engineering attack in which an attacker impersonates a trusted source to trick a person into revealing information, sending money, opening malicious content or taking another unsafe action

questions.explanation: Phishing is a social-engineering attack in which an attacker impersonates a trusted source to trick a person into revealing information, sending money, opening malicious content or taking another unsafe action.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is the main objective of phishing?

options.A: To improve network speed
options.B: To steal credentials or personal and financial information, deliver malware, obtain money or gain unauthorised access

questions.explanation: The main objective of phishing is to steal credentials or personal and financial information, deliver malware, obtain money or gain unauthorised access.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is a phishing email?

options.A: A legitimate email from a bank
options.B: A deceptive email that appears to come from a legitimate person or organisation and tries to manipulate the recipient
options.C: An email with a large attachment
options.D: An email that has been encrypted

questions.explanation: A phishing email is a deceptive email that appears to come from a legitimate person or organisation and tries to manipulate the recipient.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What are common warning signs of phishing?

options.A: Unexpected urgency, threats, unusual requests, suspicious links, unexpected attachments, mismatched sender addresses, spelling anomalies and requests for passwords or OTPs

questions.explanation: Common warning signs include unexpected urgency, threats, unusual requests, suspicious links, unexpected attachments, mismatched sender addresses, spelling anomalies and requests for passwords or OTPs.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is spear phishing?

options.A: A phishing attack sent to millions of people at once
options.B: A targeted phishing attack customised for a particular person, organisation or role
options.D: Phishing carried out through voice calls

questions.explanation: Spear phishing is a targeted phishing attack customised for a particular person, organisation or role.

questions.subject: Cybersecurity
questions.question: What is whaling?
